body.head: ELIAS HICKS,. &C.
body.p:
Prefatory Note.—As myself a little boy hearing so much of E. H., at that time, long ago, in Suffolk and Queens and Kings CountiesCounties—and more than once personally seeing and hearingϑ the old man—and my‸‸dear, dear father and mother faithful listeners to him at the meetings—I remember how I dream'd to write perhaps a piece about E. H. and his bl/ooklook and discourses, however long afterward—for my dearϑ parents' sake—and the ‸‸dear Friends too! And the following is what has at last all but
tr come out of it—the feeling and intention never forgotten yet!

There is a sort of nature of persons I have compared to little rills of water, fresh, from perennial springs—(and the comparison is indeed an appropriate one‸|,—persons not so very plenty, yet some few certainly of them running over the surface and area of humanity‸,,/ all times‸,,/ all lands.ϑ It is a specimen of this class I would now present. I would sum up in E. H.‸,/ and make his case stand for, the class, the sort, in all ages, all lands, sparse, not numerous, yet enough to irrigate the soil, enough to prove the inherent moral stock and irrepressible devotional aspirations growing indigenuϑouslyindigenously of themselves, always advancing‸,/ and never utterly gone under or lost.
